recommendation.executive_summary: CloudForge evaluated your requirements for a production web application running on Python / FastAPI. With an anticipated 250 peak concurrent users and 5000 daily active users, we recommend the 'Multi-Instance Redundant' architecture. This model prioritizes security isolation by housing compute and database workloads in private subnets behind an Application Load Balancer with SSM-managed operational access.

recommended_services.purpose: Isolated private network boundary across multi-AZ
recommended_services.configuration_details: CIDR: 10.0.0.0/16 with 2 Public Subnets & 2 Private Subnets in us-east-1.
recommended_services.rationale: Mandatory baseline isolation for cloud workloads to enforce least-privilege network routing.

recommended_services.purpose: Layer 7 Traffic Distribution and SSL/TLS Termination
recommended_services.configuration_details: Public ALB terminating HTTPS (port 443) with ACM Certificate and forwarding to private targets.
recommended_services.rationale: Terminating SSL at the ALB offloads crypto calculations from app servers and hides backend instances from direct public exposure.

recommended_services.purpose: Outbound internet access for private subnet workloads
recommended_services.configuration_details: Single NAT Gateway (dev/staging) or Dual NAT Gateways (production) in public subnets.
recommended_services.rationale: Allows backend instances in private subnets to pull container images, OS patches, and third-party APIs without accepting inbound internet connections.

recommended_services.configuration_details: 2 instance(s), 50 GB gp3 EBS root volume, IMDSv2 enforced.
recommended_services.rationale: Selected t3.large matches your target of 2 vCPU and 4 GB memory requirements with burstable/general performance.

recommended_services.configuration_details: db.t3.micro, 30 GB gp3 storage, Multi-AZ: True, automated backups: 7 days.
recommended_services.rationale: Fully managed relational database handles automated patching, replication, failover, and point-in-time snapshots far more reliably than self-hosted database on EC2.

recommended_services.purpose: Durable object storage for file uploads and static assets
recommended_services.configuration_details: Standard tier bucket with S3 Public Access Block, KMS SSE-S3 encryption, and versioning.
recommended_services.rationale: 11 9's durability with server-side encryption prevents file corruption and accidental data loss.

recommended_services.purpose: Least-privilege role-based access for EC2 instances and operations
recommended_services.configuration_details: Instance profile with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore (no open SSH port 22 needed).
recommended_services.rationale: Eliminates static hardcoded API keys on EC2 instances by utilizing IAM temporary role credentials.

recommended_services.purpose: OWASP Top 10 protection and rate limiting
recommended_services.configuration_details: Attached to ALB with AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet and SQLi rule groups.
recommended_services.rationale: Blocks common exploits, malicious crawlers, and layer 7 volumetric attacks before reaching instances.

recommended_services.purpose: Centralized metrics, alarms, and SSM Session Manager shell access
recommended_services.configuration_details: CloudWatch Agent for memory & disk metrics; Alarms on CPU > 80% and 5xx HTTP response counts.
recommended_services.rationale: Provides real-time visibility into operational health without opening bastion hosts or inbound firewall ports.

networking_and_security: Strict VPC isolation: no direct public IPs on application or database instances.
Least-privilege security groups: ingress strictly restricted to upstream components.
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for operational access without SSH key distribution or bastion hosts.
IMDSv2 enforced on all compute instances to prevent SSRF credential exfiltration.
All data encrypted at rest with AWS KMS and in transit with TLS 1.3.
disaster_recovery_plan: Multi-AZ deployment: automatic failover with RTO < 60s and RPO = 0.
Automated database snapshots retained for 7 days.
Cross-region AMI copy recommended if multi-region disaster recovery is required.
monitoring_and_logging: CloudWatch Metrics: EC2 CPUUtilization, DiskReadOps, NetworkIn/Out.
CloudWatch Alarms: Trigger alert at CPU > 80% for 5 minutes.
ALB HTTP 5xx error rate monitoring with Slack/Email notifications via Amazon SNS.
AWS CloudTrail enabled across all regions for audit logging of management events.

alternatives.description: Cost-optimized single-instance setup with public subnet and single-AZ RDS.
tradeoffs: No Multi-AZ failover (brief downtime during maintenance or AZ outages)
No Application Load Balancer (direct instance exposure)
Single point of failure on the app server

alternatives.description: Resilient dual-AZ deployment with private app instances, ALB, and managed RDS.
tradeoffs: Requires NAT gateway for private egress

alternatives.description: Multi-AZ Aurora Cluster with ECS Fargate containers, Auto Scaling, and CloudFront CDN.
tradeoffs: Greater configuration and CI/CD orchestration complexity

risks_and_bottlenecks: Database connection pooling: ensure your application runtime utilizes connection pooling (e.g., PgBouncer or SQLAlchemy pool) to avoid exhausting RDS connections.
NAT Gateway outbound egress bandwidth: intensive outbound API calls or downloads incur $0.045/GB transfer costs.
Single-AZ database risk: if Multi-AZ is disabled, an underlying AWS hardware failure can cause 15-45 minutes of unplanned database recovery time.

Load Testing Disclaimer: This architecture is a structured recommendation based on stated parameters. It does NOT guarantee performance under arbitrary load until validated with synthetic load testing (e.g. k6, Locust).
step_by_step_implementation_plan: Step 1: Deploy VPC, Internet Gateway, Public Subnets, Private Subnets, and NAT Gateway via CloudForge Terraform module.
Step 2: Provision Security Groups enforcing strict ingress: ALB allows 80/443; EC2 allows only ALB ingress; RDS allows only EC2 security group ingress.
Step 3: Provision Amazon RDS instance in private database subnet group and securely store master credentials in AWS Secrets Manager.
Step 4: Provision Amazon S3 bucket with versioning and default KMS encryption; attach least-privilege IAM policy to the EC2 Instance Profile.
Step 5: Launch EC2 instances in private subnets utilizing the CloudForge template with IMDSv2 and SSM Agent enabled.
Step 6: Configure Application Load Balancer target groups with health checks (e.g. GET /health) and associate ACM TLS certificate.
Step 7: Configure CloudWatch alarms for CPU > 80%, Memory > 85%, and RDS FreeStorageSpace < 5 GB.
